question.text: SEBI has mandated an Investor Charter for AIFs. Which of the following is a right guaranteed to AIF investors under this charter?

answer.text: Right to guaranteed minimum returns of 10% per annum
Right to direct the fund manager on specific investments to make
Right to receive periodic disclosures including financial information, portfolio details, and material changes in the fund
Right to withdraw capital at any time without penalty

explanation.text: The Logic: Investor reporting requirements include portfolio/company, sector, performance, significant development, deal-pipeline and exit information, and the Investor Charter covers services, grievance redressal, and investor responsibilities. The keyed option captures this periodic-disclosure framing. The Trap: Option A invents a return guarantee, which AIFs cannot provide. Option B gives investors direct investment control, which is inconsistent with the fund-manager mandate. Option D would override the closed-ended/lock-in structure of typical AIFs. Note: The Investor Charter focuses on disclosure, grievance redressal and fair treatment rather than on absolute or unconditional commercial rights.
